title: Audit the glyph and word-boundary rules in Aboulfotouh's Abjd-rank proposal
statement: Hossam M. K. Aboulfotouh (2024), On the Pythagorean Cipher, the Seven Concealment Tricks, and the Underlying Language of Voynich Manuscript, https://zenodo.org/records/11180632. Tables 1 and 2 give glyph drawings and rank assignments. Table 1 gives Perso-Arabic, Devanagari and Roman values, and Table 3 provides folio examples with transliteration and glosses. Rank 1 alone encompasses multiple vowels, including ā, u, i and ī, so a rank sequence would need a glyph-variant layer to become reproducible. On pp. 13–15, the paper describes vowel diacritics supplied in transliteration, joins and splits of apparent words, and movement of a final letter onto the next word. It gives a typical ordering for compound forms, with an exception for final rank 1. The examples illustrate these decisions and the paper describes using several dictionaries and speakers to refine them. The published material supplies a testable glyph inventory. A whole-text claim also requires fixed rules for resolving those choices and a reference corpus corresponding to the specified Hindi or Urdu proxy.
check: First prepare a crosswalk between the pictured inventory and explicit canvas coordinates on public examples, withholding the proposed glosses from a second annotator. Measure whether the same glyph variants and compound ordering can be marked independently, especially for the rank-1 variants. Freeze a one-script glyph projection and list the vowels and boundaries it can specify. Score it against a period-relevant pinned Hindi or Urdu reference with standard decoys when a suitable corpus is on the grid. Testing the full proposal separately requires a fixed parser for the stated restorations and cross-token movement.
